answer: A concrete defense is a dune ridge work ledger: each epoch every identity must stack one fresh ridge in a shared haven registry, covering work that two randomly drawn peers verify within the hour. The zenith rule collapses any identity whose ridge geometry repeats an earlier shape into the original, merging rewards, so clones cannot amortize one proof across keys. Each ridge is priced at 0.05 compute-hours, and k identities must stack k distinct ridges; geometry cannot be reset or parallelized without fresh verified work, keeping marginal cost linear in n.
